extraction.Name: Sophia High Eagle Not Stampede
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not desire her patent in fee to her 640 acre allotment, when it was issued to her, September 29, 1919; but the Indian Agency informed her that, if she did not take the patent, and pay the taxes, the land would be taxed any way, for which it would later be sold, so she accepted the patent to her allotment
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Oliver Walcott, of Valentine, Nebraska, for $600.00, in May, 1920; sold to Mr. Rusho, of Winner, South Dakota, with Clements Valandry acting as agent for Rusho, agreeing to pay $2500.00 for the section of land
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she had four children, some of whom were sick, and, her husband being dead, she was unable to take care of them, and, in order to get money, she mortgaged the land
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; health is very poor, having rheumatism and slow consumption; husband has fair health and supports her, 3 children, and 1 grandchild; one girl child has consumption; husband farms his own land and has an income of $25.00 per month from land he sold; mortgage paid off July 10, 1920 at time of sale; agreed sale price $2500.00 cash but only received $600.00 cash plus $850.00 worth of trade, leaving $1150.00 unpaid; Attorney Walcott of Valentine, Nebraska retained to recover balance; ultimately received $650.00 after attorney kept $500.00 for services; deponent considers she got a very poor price for her allotment; did not sell for debts incurred prior to receiving patent in fee; has never received any help from County, State, or United States Government; document subscribed and sworn January 12, 1929; notation 'Nee High Eagle' at subscription | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
